name: Le Long Dinh
role: Last king of the Early Lê, whose death in 1009 opened the way for Lý Công Uẩn.
known_facts: Son of Lê Hoàn (Lê Đại Hành); took the throne in 1005 after his brother Lê Long Việt was killed.
Called Lê Ngọa Triều in the histories, which record notorious cruelty and excess.
Died in 1009 at about twenty-four, leaving young sons.
His death created the succession crisis that brought Lý Công Uẩn to power.
interpretation: A slight, pale Vietnamese man of about twenty-three, round-faced, heavy brows over restless eyes, a thin moustache, hair in a topknot under a gold-fitted cap. He wears a crimson silk robe embroidered with gold thread, wide sleeves, a heavy gold belt and gold arm-rings, with a curved ivory-handled dagger at his hip.
